note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative. Times are fictional labels. The scene depicts the supplied order of the messages only; it never states when a withdrawal takes effect, whether a message arrived in time, which one prevails, or whether the proposal is revoked or still open.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional proposal to supply chairs. The withdrawal message is sent after the proposal and, as supplied, is received before it; the hold shows the supplied state: withdrawal communicated (as supplied).

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: a garden-services proposal; different parties; the two receipts are supplied with the same position, so the strip shows them together as an order to be examined, and the hold brackets the time sequence as to be examined.

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long names, roles and time labels, three terms, four events and two annotations. Standing coordinator rule item 20 (caps with the true reason). The pre-cap values are kept in LAW-0449.presets.precap.json. Each capped field was restored alone to its pre-cap value on top of the shipped preset and rendered (layout verdict, text px, smallest rendered head): proposal reference 13 -> 22 characters: 1:1 has no layout (the two stacked message cards make the racks too tall for the hands to reach; best 16.1 px, heads 50.8 px, flagged). Withdrawal reference 13 -> 24: the same at 1:1. Proposal title 45 -> 79: no layout at 9:16 (the strip no longer fits between the rows) or 1:1 (racks too tall). Item term 41 -> 52: no layout at 1:1. Quantity term 26 -> 33: no layout at 9:16. Annotations 40 -> 72 and 34 -> 54: at 1:1 neither annotation finds a place next to its target or in the band. With every capped field restored: 16:9 fits at 16.1 px; 9:16 and 1:1 have no layout. The delivery term (39) and the withdrawal text (79) are no longer capped. Every capped value stays longer than baseline; names, roles, time labels and every count (3 terms, 4 events, 2 annotations) are kept.
